search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting influenza (flu) cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and surveillance data for the United States during the week of 2024-09-29 to 2024-10-05, covering national and subnational breakdowns.
search_reasoning: The target window (Sept 29 – Oct 5, 2024) falls at the very start of the 2024–2025 U.S. influenza season. The CDC's FluView weekly surveillance system is the primary authoritative source for U.S. flu data, publishing weekly reports keyed to MMWR epidemiological weeks. MMWR Week 40 (ending Oct 5, 2024) is the most relevant reporting unit. Secondary sources include WHO/PAHO global flu updates, state health department reports, and news coverage citing official figures. Upstream queries used overly literal date-range strings embedded in quoted phrases (e.g., "2024-09-29-2024-10-05"), which are unlikely to match real document text. This iteration replaces those with operationally realistic queries: CDC FluView week-40 terminology, MMWR week references, and season-start framing. The 4-query cap per iteration is respected. Queries are distributed across the highest-value channels: official site search (CDC/FluView), web search (WHO/PAHO + news), and a structured-database/surveillance query.

query_batch.query: CDC FluView influenza surveillance weekly report "week 40" OR "week ending October 5" 2024 United States cases hospitalizations deaths
query_batch.query_rationale: CDC FluView is the definitive U.S. influenza surveillance system. MMWR Week 40 (ending Oct 5, 2024) is the precise epidemiological week covering the task window. This query targets the weekly FluView report with season-start and MMWR-week terminology that will actually appear in CDC document titles and text, unlike the upstream literal date-range strings.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC FluView weekly surveillance report for MMWR Week 40, 2024; expect tables of ILI activity, hospitalization rates, and mortality indicators by state/region
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; FluView branding; MMWR week numbering; official CDC authorship

query_batch.query: CDC influenza "2024-2025 season" "MMWR week 40" OR "October 2024" surveillance activity level United States
query_batch.query_rationale: Complementary CDC query using season framing ('2024-2025 season') and MMWR week 40 reference to capture FluView dashboard pages, situation updates, or MMWR early-release notes that may use slightly different titling than the main weekly report.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: CDC FluView interactive dashboard summary, MMWR early-release, or CDC situation update for week 40 of the 2024-2025 flu season
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: cdc.gov domain; MMWR citation; official CDC authorship

query_batch.query: WHO PAHO influenza update United States "October 2024" OR "week 40 2024" cases deaths surveillance report
query_batch.query_rationale: WHO and PAHO publish weekly global and regional influenza updates that include U.S. data, providing independent corroboration of CDC figures. October 2024 framing aligns with the task window without relying on literal date-range strings.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: WHO Global Influenza Surveillance and Response System (GISRS) weekly update or PAHO Epidemiological Alert/Update for the Americas, week 40 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: who.int or paho.org domain; official WHO/PAHO authorship; epidemiological week numbering

query_batch.query: influenza flu season start United States "late September" OR "early October 2024" cases hospitalizations deaths report
query_batch.query_rationale: News coverage from late September to early October 2024 may cite official CDC or state health department figures on flu season onset, providing evidence quotes, subnational location detail, and corroborating case/death counts for the task window. This query avoids literal date-range strings and uses natural-language temporal framing that news articles would actually use.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: News articles from major outlets (AP, Reuters, NPR, local health desks) citing CDC or state health department flu figures for the week of Sept 29 – Oct 5, 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Publication date within Sept 29 – Oct 12, 2024; explicit citation of CDC FluView or state health department; quantitative case/hospitalization figures

expected_evidence: CDC FluView weekly report for MMWR Week 40 (week ending October 5, 2024) with ILI activity levels, hospitalization rates, and mortality data by U.S. region and state
CDC FluView dashboard or situation update citing confirmed/unspecified influenza cases and hospitalizations for week 40, 2024-2025 season

language_or_localization_reasoning: All queries are in English. The United States is an English-language jurisdiction. CDC FluView, MMWR, WHO, and PAHO all publish primary U.S. influenza surveillance data in English. No localization to other languages is required for this task.
trust_considerations: Prioritize sources with explicit MMWR week 40 or 'week ending October 5, 2024' references to confirm temporal alignment with the task window
CDC FluView is the gold-standard source; any figures from news or international sources should be cross-checked against FluView data

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 (only iter1_q1 was executed out of 4 planned queries) successfully identified the primary CDC FluView Week 40 report and a Mississippi state-level PDF — both directly covering the task window (Sept 29 – Oct 5, 2024). However, three planned queries (iter1_q2, iter1_q3, iter1_q4) were never executed. Key gaps remain: (1) no WHO/PAHO international corroboration, (2) no news-source evidence quotes, (3) no additional state-level subnational data beyond Mississippi, (4) no pediatric mortality or hospitalization rate data confirmed from a second source, and (5) the H5N1 California cases mentioned in the Week 40 snippet warrant a targeted follow-up. One more iteration with up to 4 queries will close these gaps and satisfy the stop condition (primary CDC source confirmed + at least one corroborating international or news source).
